chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Two men do not inherit from each other if one of them killed the other."
ai.seo_question: Can a murderer inherit from the person they killed according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *Ghulul* (exclusion) in Shia jurisprudence, where a killer is barred from inheriting from their victim to prevent unjust enrichment. While the primary chain emphasizes the direct killer, Shia scholars often extend this ruling to include the killer's heirs in cases of *Qatl al-Khas* (specific murder), ensuring the estate remains with the rightful lineage. This rule complements the Quranic concept of *Diyya* and *Qisas*, prioritizing justice over mere financial gain.
